content: The book titled Welfare, Choice and Solidarity in Transition: Reforming the Health Sector in Eastern Europe was authored by János Kornai and Karen Eggleston and published in 2001. It examines the health sector reforms in ten post-socialist Eastern European countries, specifically Albania, Bulgaria, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Hungary, the Republic of Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. As of 2007, based on the World Bank's classification, these ten countries were categorized into different income groups. Albania was classified as a lower-middle-income economy. The Czech Republic and Slovenia were categorized as high-income economies. The remaining countries—Bulgaria, Croatia, Hungary, the Republic of Macedonia, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia—were classified as upper-middle-income economies.
